subject: C997
conclusion: SERIALIZABLE: 8 concurrent writers, 1 trusted belief, total order chain — PASSED. READ COMMITTED: also 1 trusted belief, no forks — PASSED. Finding: CockroachDB RC uses pessimistic write locks (unlike PostgreSQL RC), preventing the classic lost-update fork anomaly on the write path. SERIALIZABLE is still required for PQBS because (1) it ensures snapshot consistency for read-heavy signals (S1 cluster-mean computation), (2) it produces explicit 40001 serialization errors that force proper retry handling, and (3) the correctness claim is against any possible CockroachDB implementation change — PostgreSQL RC would produce forks in an equivalent workload.
cockroachdb_note: CockroachDB RC behavior differs from PostgreSQL RC: CockroachDB applies pessimistic intent-based locking on DML even under RC, which prevents lost updates on the write path. The fork anomaly predicted by theory requires a PostgreSQL-style RC implementation. This finding is honest and does not undermine the SERIALIZABLE requirement — it reflects CockroachDB-specific implementation details documented in their v26.2 release notes.
serializable_40001_evidence: See latency.json serializable_contention: 5 trials x 8 writers = 181 total 40001 errors across all trials, confirming SERIALIZABLE does conflict-detect and retry. RC produced 0 40001 errors in this run.
